headline: Chinese lidar maker Hesai has launched a camera and cloud service that turns real rooms into 3D scenes for training robots.
score_reason: Fresh product launch, but a company announcement with company-supplied results.
importance_line: Robot developers may get cheaper realistic training scenes, but all speed and success figures come from Hesai.
summary: Unite.AI reports, citing Hesai's launch event, that Chinese lidar (laser-sensor) maker Hesai introduced Kosmo, a spatial camera and cloud platform that scans real places into 3D scenes used to train robots and build world models. Hesai says a room can be scanned in about 15 minutes instead of roughly 300 hours of manual modelling, a company claim that has not been independently checked.
notes: Pool link was Reuters (blocked, 401); read Unite.AI. Reuters headline confirms the story.
